text: # Wave-end review

Roster by wave type: critic-reviewer always; alignment-officer and docs-sync when a plan or phase doc exists; domain-reviewer for domain work; anomaly-hunter when the wave produced a new measurement (skip on pure bug-fix or doc-only waves); inventory-auditor when the wave added capability; lean-critic, always, on the wave's diff (it preloads ponytail); pragmatism-officer last, once findings exist; then retro-officer, always, as the final step: give it the ledger path, the findings (files or reports), the commit range per repo and the main transcript path (`~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session id>.jsonl`).
It appends one entry to `docs/retros/retro-log.md` in the config repo.

**Analysis-wave trial (owner 2026-11-08, next 3 analysis waves, then decide):** a wave whose output is a measurement or finding, not code, runs domain-reviewer, anomaly-hunter and pragmatism-officer; critic-reviewer only when the wave changed a gate or test; lean-critic, inventory-auditor and docs-sync only at a doc-heavy close; retro-officer as always, recording "trial n/3" and any later finding a dropped seat would have caught.
Code waves keep the roster above.

Dispatch in batches under the concurrency cap (2 on the smaller account, 3 on the larger), science seats first (domain-reviewer, anomaly-hunter), then critic-reviewer and alignment-officer, then docs-sync, inventory-auditor and lean-critic, so governance text is drafted after the findings it must not contradict.
The review is pinned to one commit (its HEAD is named in the close); commits after it, such as features the owner adds at review, get a short second critic pass before merge.
A spawn refused at the cap is not queued: re-dispatch it when a slot frees.
The close lists every seat as ran or not-ran, with the reason.
Findings files go in the findings dir (`.superpowers/findings/<date>/` in the config repo, persistent), never the scratchpad, which dies with the job.

A seat is not "ran" until its findings file has its closing section (`command grep -q '^## CLOSING' <file>`) and `wave_stats.py` lists it under no `turn_limit_by_seat`; a truncated seat or a `Not covered` entry is re-dispatched on those areas, not accepted; if a seat put findings only in its message, re-run it; only as a last resort write them into its file, marked controller-written, before closing.
When the wave's evidence is only self-consistency, say so in the close and keep a standing row for one held-out evaluation.

A branch that is not merged, or whose full suite could not run, carries the line "MERGE GATE: full suite on the merge commit, job spec written" in its ledger and plan status, with the job spec's path; the wave is not marked closed without that line.

Nothing that says built, verified, merged, closed, answered or resolved (status docs, findings, commit subjects, headline prose in FINDINGS, replies to the owner) is written or pushed before the roster has run and the close line exists; before that it says "candidate" with its measurement, or is marked DRAFT (a headline is not a status doc, so this failed 4 times); "push at wave end" means after that line, and a /compact keep-line says "push after review close" (R-20261030-1/-9:
SenC and MeMES pushed claims hours before the review, one headline later retracted).
A post-refresh test failure recorded in a handoff becomes a ledger item with an owner and the next refresh as its gate, never only a note.
A ledger deferral saying a gate, guard or fixture "passes on" a default, "has no true case" or is unvalidated is not deferrable: it becomes a register row or a re-open, and the step is not GREEN.
A CI check that is red with no job log (minutes exhausted) is recorded as not run; the PR carries the local equivalent's command and output.

**Aim check, after the retro.** Before any new wave or fix round, dispatch `aim-keeper` with the project path, the wave's Goal line and commit range, and the next step on the table (say whether the owner or Claude proposed it).
